question: A 25-year-old man presents with jaw discomfort and the inability to open his mouth fully for about 3 days. About a week ago, he says he cut himself while preparing a chicken dinner but did not seek medical assistance. Five days after the original injury, he started noticing jaw discomfort and an inability to open his mouth completely. He has no history of a serious illness or allergies and takes no medications. The patient says he had received his primary tetanus series in childhood, and that his last booster was more than 10 years ago. His blood pressure is 125/70 mm Hg and temperature is 36.9℃ (98.5°F). On physical examination, the patient is unable to open his jaw wider than 2.5 cm. Head and neck examinations are otherwise unremarkable. There is a 5 cm linear shallow laceration with some granulation tissue on the right index finger without necrosis, erythema, or pus. After wound care and initiation of metronidazole, which of the following is the next best step in the management of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has a history of a cut" -> "Cut occurred while preparing food" -> "Injury is potentially contaminated" -> "Jaw discomfort and limited opening suggest possible infection" -> "Patient's last tetanus booster was over 10 years ago" -> "Current guidelines recommend Td booster for wounds" -> "Td is appropriate for this patient" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with jaw discomfort" -> "Inability to open mouth suggests trismus" -> "Trismus can be associated with tetanus" -> "Patient's last tetanus booster was over 10 years ago" -> "Tdap is recommended for adults who have not had it in 10 years" -> "Tdap provides protection against tetanus" -> "Tdap is appropriate for this patient" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has a laceration on finger" -> "Laceration is shallow with no signs of infection" -> "Jaw discomfort may indicate tetanus exposure" -> "Patient's last tetanus booster was over 10 years ago" -> "Td booster is indicated for prevention" -> "Td is appropriate for this patient" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of a cut" -> "Cut is on the finger and not directly related to jaw" -> "Jaw discomfort may indicate another issue" -> "Patient's tetanus vaccination status is outdated" -> "Tdap is recommended for adults every 10 years" -> "Tdap is appropriate for this patient" -> 75%
analysis: The patient has a history of a cut and presents with jaw discomfort and trismus, which raises suspicion for tetanus, especially given his last booster was over 10 years ago. The appropriate management includes administering a tetanus booster. Since he has had his primary series and the last booster was more than 10 years ago, he should receive a Td (tetanus-diphtheria) booster. Tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG) is indicated for high-risk wounds in unimmunized patients or those with unknown vaccination status, but this patient is not in that category. Therefore, the next best step is to administer Td.
